labeller_quality_evaluated: yes = the labeller's own output is scored against gold/manually annotated data on data not used to tune it
partial = only a component is scored, or scoring is on the set used to develop/tune the labelling functions, or only the labeller-as-model (not the emitted training labels) is scored
no = no gold-referenced evaluation of the labeller itself is reported (only the downstream model, or nothing)
comparator_codes: chance = an explicit random / chance / zero-skill baseline is reported as a comparator
majority_class = an explicit majority-class (or all-positive/all-negative) baseline is reported
metadata_only = a comparator built only from structured data, metadata, ICD/billing/Z codes or other non-text features
simpler_text_model = a weaker text model or rule/regex baseline
human_iaa = a human inter-annotator agreement statistic is reported
other_labeller = a different automatic labeller (or a human labeller) is compared
gold_supervised = a model trained on manual gold labels is compared (added code; not in the original request vocabulary but the single most common comparator)
none = no comparator is reported for the labelling/extraction stage
coding_vocabulary.coding_rule_generosity: Comparators are coded as present if they appear ANYWHERE in the paper (labeller-level or downstream-model-level). This is deliberately generous to the papers and therefore conservative with respect to the claim under test.

coding_provenance.method: Each record was coded from the paper's full text (Europe PMC fullTextXML, PMC HTML, ar5iv HTML, or ACL Anthology landing page) using a fixed 7-item coding prompt that required a verbatim supporting quote or the token UNCLEAR for every item.
coding_provenance.known_limitation: No second rater and no inter-coder agreement statistic; the coding is therefore subject to exactly the kind of unquantified labelling error this survey is about. Quotes are retained in the notes field so any item can be re-checked against the source.

records.title: Ontology-driven weak supervision for clinical entity classification in electronic health records
records.labeller_type: ontology labelling functions + Snorkel label model
records.labeller_eval_evidence: Word-level precision of one ontology source reported ('only had 65% word-level precision'); label-model source accuracies estimated without ground truth; no systematic per-source gold evaluation.
records.statistical_test: two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank, alpha 0.05
records.gold_positives_value: test-set entity counts per benchmark (e.g. ShARe/CLEF disorder 7367; BC5CDR chemical 5385); COVID case study positives not reported
records.notes: Human gold annotations were adjudicated but no agreement statistic reported.

records.title: Weakly supervised language models for automated extraction of critical findings from radiology reports
records.labeller_type: LLM (Mistral-7B-Instruct / BioMistral-7B, zero- and few-shot) matched to a SNOMED-expanded term list
records.labeller_eval_evidence: The prompted LLMs (the labellers) are scored on the gold test sets as 'PT' baselines, but the weak labels actually emitted on the 15,000 training reports are not evaluated.
records.statistical_test: none ('Error bars denote standard deviations.')
records.gold_positives_value: 15 (Mayo); 50 (MIMIC-III)
records.notes: Cohen kappa 0.738 (MIMIC-III) and 0.798 (Mayo) reported for the human annotation, not as a performance comparator.

records.title: Leveraging large language models for knowledge-free weak supervision in clinical natural language processing
records.labeller_type: LLM (Llama2-13B few-shot; optionally fine-tuned) generating weak token labels
records.labeller_eval_evidence: Weak-label counts, entities per sentence and post-processing failure rates are reported; no precision/recall/F1 for the weak labels themselves. Performance is reported only for the downstream BERT models.
records.statistical_test: none
records.notes: Gold notes were selected to have entity counts near the median, which is a sampling rule, not a power calculation.

records.title: Weakly supervised spatial relation extraction from radiology reports
records.labeller_type: 19 labelling functions (RadLex dictionaries, regex, heuristics) + Snorkel label model
records.labeller_eval_evidence: 'The LFs are developed and refined in iteration by evaluating on the annotated Rad-SpDev set' - the labeller is scored on the set used to tune it, so this is not a held-out labeller evaluation.
comparator_names: fully supervised BERT-LARGE-MIMIC from prior work
records.statistical_test: none (average F1 over 10-fold CV, no CI or test)
records.prevalence_value: 358/400 reports contain spatial relations (89.5%) at report level; trigger-level prevalence not stated
records.gold_positives_value: frame-element counts total 3131 but scope of the count is not defined
records.notes: Single physician annotated the development reports; no agreement statistic.

records.venue: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making
records.title: A clinical text classification paradigm using weak supervision and deep representation
records.text_domain: clinical notes (smoking status, hip fracture, i2b2)
records.labeller_type: rule-based NLP algorithm (keywords/regex) generating training labels
records.labeller_eval_evidence: 'Table 4 shows the results of the proposed paradigm compared with the rule-based NLP algorithms in the three case studies' - the rule labeller's P/R/F1 is reported on the manually annotated test sets.
records.statistical_test: t-test at 5% level
records.notes: Test-set sizes given (475, 498, 79) without class breakdown for the evaluation sets.

records.title: Weakly supervised natural language processing for assessing patient-centered outcome following prostate cancer treatment
records.labeller_type: domain dictionaries (64 UI terms, 48 BD terms) + NegEx/CLEVER building an artificial training set
records.labeller_eval_evidence: Only the pipeline's sentence-extraction step is validated ('we randomly selected 100 narratives from both cohorts and achieved 97% accuracy with manual validation'); agreement of the dictionary labels with manual annotation is not reported.
records.statistical_test: significance claimed for the sentence-level comparison with Naive Bayes; test not named
records.prevalence_value: class distribution deferred to a supplementary table
records.gold_positives_value: gold set described as 110 notes / 120 sentences without per-class counts
records.notes: Companion study to Gori 2019 (EGEMS) from the same group and same dictionaries; see sensitivity analysis in survey_findings.md.

records.title: A probabilistic approach for building disease phenotypes across electronic health records
records.labeller_type: labelling functions aggregated by majority vote, Snorkel OSS, or LEVI (labels are the pipeline output)
records.labeller_eval_evidence: 'resulting in a total of 800 patients with ground truth labels' from physician chart review; aggregated labels scored against them with bootstrap CIs.
records.statistical_test: none; 95% bootstrap confidence intervals only
records.prevalence_value: 26% overall
records.gold_positives_value: ~208 (26% of 800), not stated directly
records.notes: 'Majority Vote' here is LF aggregation, not a majority-class baseline.

records.title: Use of noisy labels as weak learners to identify incompletely ascertainable outcomes: A Feasibility study with opioid-induced respiratory depression
records.labeller_type: 14 expert labelling functions in Snorkel; generative model emits probabilistic labels
records.labeller_eval_evidence: 'the empirical accuracy of individual LFs ranged 0.47-1.00'; the generative model is scored against manual adjudication on validation and test sets.
records.statistical_test: none; nested CV range 0.6-0.8 reported, not a CI
records.notes: One of only seven records with a genuine non-text comparator (AHRQ PSI-11), and the only one where a 0.83% prevalence gold set with 5 positives is used to certify a labeller without any uncertainty quantification.

records.venue: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making
records.title: Automatic de-identification of French electronic health records: a cost-effective approach exploiting distant supervision and deep learning models
records.labeller_type: rules + dictionaries + national knowledge bases + record metadata (distant supervision)
records.labeller_eval_evidence: 'The rule-based system achieves interesting results, with an F1 score of 0.9365' on the manually annotated test set; the automatically generated training labels are not separately scored.
records.statistical_test: none for model comparisons; 95% CI reported for Fleiss kappa only (0.93, 0.922-0.939)
records.gold_positives_value: 5726 entity mentions (micro-average support)
records.notes: Manual annotation was pre-annotated with the rule-based output, which the paper notes but does not analyse; the abstract uses the word 'significant' with no test.

records.venue: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making
records.title: Ontology-driven and weakly supervised rare disease identification from clinical notes
records.labeller_type: two rule-based labelling functions (mention length; concept prevalence) combined with AND
records.labeller_eval_evidence: Only the downstream confirmation model is evaluated; 'the evaluation set is independent of the rules used for weak supervision' but the accuracy of the weak labels is not reported.
comparator_names: baseline purely based on manual ICD codes
records.statistical_test: none; authors decline to draw conclusions from small subsets
records.prevalence_value: MIMIC-III discharge summaries: validation 142/400 = 35.5%; test 187/673 = 27.8%
records.gold_positives_value: 142 (validation) + 187 (test) = 329 for MIMIC-III discharge summaries; positives for the other two sets not reported
records.notes: Multi-rater kappa 0.76/0.72/0.88/0.86 reported. Explicitly notes the small test sample but gives no MDE.

records.title: Leveraging weak supervision to perform named entity recognition in electronic health records progress notes to identify the ophthalmology exam
records.labeller_type: distant supervision from paired structured SmartForm entries, aligned to note tokens (IOB2)
records.labeller_eval_evidence: 'evaluated against human annotations was high (0.96)' on 100 notes.
records.statistical_test: none; point estimates only
records.notes: The structured SmartForm data is the label source, not a comparator, so it is not coded as a metadata-only baseline.

records.title: Improving ascertainment of suicidal ideation and suicide attempt with natural language processing
records.labeller_type: rule/IR-based weak labelling: seed manual labels at probability 1, rank-decaying probabilities, max-combined with ICD-derived probabilities
records.labeller_eval_evidence: 'we assumed each patient from this initial set was labeled as a case or non-case with high confidence'; AUPRC and P@K are reported for the ranker but the unreviewed assigned labels are not validated against held-out gold.
records.statistical_test: bootstrap 95% CIs (1000 replicates) for AUPRC; unnamed test of ICD-code proportions across ranked quartiles (p<2.2e-16)
records.prevalence_value: not reported as a single figure; 200-patient ICD validation precision 96% (SI) / 85% (SA)
records.gold_positives_value: 921 (SI) and 682 (SA) manual-validation cases
records.notes: The ICD comparator is partly the label source (ICD probabilities enter the weak label), so it is not an independent alternative explanation.

records.venue: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making
records.title: Classifying the lifestyle status for Alzheimer's disease from clinical notes using deep learning with weak supervision
records.labeller_type: rule-based keyword classifier with negation and a 5-token window
records.labeller_eval_evidence: 'The rule-based model used for weak supervision was tested on the GSC for comparison.' The accuracy of the weak labels on the training data is not separately reported.
records.statistical_test: none; mean over three seeds
records.prevalence_value: physical activity 78 vs inactivity 122 of 200 sentences (39%/61%); positive class not defined
records.gold_positives_value: per-class sentence counts given (78, 122, 18, 20, 20, 18, 12); no positive-class definition
records.notes: Cohen kappa reported as 1.0 between all annotator pairs.

records.title: Development and multicenter validation of chest X-ray radiography interpretations based on natural language processing
records.text_domain: chest X-ray reports used to label images
records.labeller_type: BERT entity/relation extraction over report text, radiologist-amended into 25 labels
records.labeller_eval_evidence: Only a qualitative check is described ('One radiologist ... recorded and checked the BERT-extracted labels'); no precision/recall of the labeller against gold. Limitation acknowledged: 'there may be errors in radiology reports and label extraction.'
records.statistical_test: DeLong test for AUC comparison; bootstrap 95% CIs (100 iterations)
records.gold_positives_value: 2686 / 206 / 802 (any-sign); per-label positives not in main text
records.notes: Large sample justified by low incidence, but no power calculation.

records.venue: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making
records.title: Multi-label annotation of text reports from computed tomography of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis using deep learning
records.labeller_type: dictionary-based rule-based algorithms (one per organ system)
records.labeller_eval_evidence: 'we manually validated the quality of the RBA labels'; however 'The RNN was tested against a test set of 48,758 reports labeled by RBA', i.e. the downstream model is evaluated against the labeller rather than against gold.
records.statistical_test: none named; DeLong confidence intervals reported
records.prevalence_value: per-label positive counts against 2158 reports (Table 1)
records.gold_positives_value: per-label # Pos (e.g. atelectasis 251, nodule 296, dilatation 87)
records.notes: Gold labels from a single annotator with no agreement statistic. Notable case of a downstream model certified against labeller output, not gold.

records.title: Weakly Semi-supervised phenotyping using Electronic Health records
records.labeller_type: unsupervised silver labels (MAP) or lab-derived rules
records.labeller_eval_evidence: 'the AUCs of MAP in classifying ARDS, Pseudogout and COPD are only 0.52, 0.59 and 0.64' - the silver labeller is scored against gold, and in one case is barely above chance.
records.statistical_test: none; 5-fold CV with 100 bootstrap replicates, no CI or test reported
records.prevalence_value: 16.4%-79.0% across MGB phenotypes; Pseudogout 21.9%; ARDS 40.9%
records.notes: Rare counter-example where the silver labeller's AUC of 0.52 (i.e. essentially chance) is explicitly reported; a conflict between the text (1.9%, n=100) and Table 1 (n=44) is noted.

records.title: ARCH: Large-scale knowledge graph via aggregated narrative codified health records analysis
records.labeller_type: PheNorm silver phenotype scores; SIDER database distant supervision for drug-side-effect pairs
records.labeller_eval_evidence: 'validated against 187, 138, 154, 127, 114, 540, 285 and 540 labeled observations' curated by manual chart review.
records.statistical_test: p-values for phenotyping differences; BH-FDR for edge testing; 95% CIs for survival
records.null_stated: partly (null of an unlinked pair for the edge test)
records.prevalence_value: 50% for the drug side-effect evaluation set, by construction
records.gold_positives_value: 128,220 database-derived drug-AE pairs; chart-reviewed counts listed but not split by class
records.notes: BORDERLINE scope: a knowledge-graph paper in which automatic label sources are promoted into a pipeline. One of only two records with any random/chance comparator, and there it is used for relation detection, not for certifying the phenotype labeller. Uses the word 'power' in the FDR-sensitivity sense, not as a design calculation.

records.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association
records.title: Distantly supervised biomedical relation extraction using piecewise attentive convolutional neural network and reinforcement learning
records.labeller_type: distant supervision from UMLS / DrugBank / IntAct triples via MetaMap
records.labeller_eval_evidence: The distant-supervision labels are not scored against gold. Only the RL denoising step is checked: 'we manually checked 400 instances that were selected as FP instances by the RL agent' (72.8% accuracy).
comparator_names: UMLS vs SemMedDB as label source (appendix)
records.statistical_test: none; 'significant improvement' claimed with no test
records.prevalence_value: may-prevent 34.8%, may-treat 43.3%, DDI 10.7%, AIMed 17.1%, BioInfer 26.2%, HPRD50 37.6%, IEPA 41.0%, LLL 49.7%
records.notes: The 'w/o multichannel (random)' ablation uses random embeddings, not a chance classifier.

records.title: Improving broad-coverage medical entity linking with semantic type prediction and large-scale datasets
records.labeller_type: distant supervision: exact-match linking of mentions to MeSH headers (PubMedDS) and Wikipedia links to UMLS (WikiMed)
records.labeller_eval_evidence: 'we randomly sampled 100 links from WikiMed for manual verification'; PubMedDS 'precision of around 84%' against overlapping manually annotated corpora. Both checks are small and recall is not assessed for WikiMed.
records.statistical_test: paired bootstrap significance testing (p<0.01)
records.notes: Three authors reviewed the 100-link sample and resolved disagreements, but no agreement statistic is reported.

records.title: Multi-task weak supervision enables anatomically-resolved abnormality detection in whole-body FDG-PET/CT
records.text_domain: PET/CT reports used to label scans
records.labeller_type: regex tagging functions + fine-tuned BERT report model + ontology probability propagation
records.labeller_eval_evidence: 'evaluating weak labels emitted by our labeling framework against hand labels' (mean AUROC 90.0%, F1 0.522-0.666 vs the regex baseline).
comparator_names: fully supervised model on hand labels
Cox model on age + summary code + indication (mortality endpoint only)
records.statistical_test: paired permutation tests; bootstrapped 95% CIs
records.notes: Chance is mentioned informally ('the fully supervised model is no better than random' in nine regions) but no chance baseline is reported as a comparator. The non-text Cox model applies to the mortality endpoint, not to abnormality labelling. Hand-label count inconsistent in the text (400 vs 391).

records.title: Using weak supervision and deep learning to classify clinical notes for identification of current suicidal ideation
records.labeller_type: rule-based NegEx lexicon labeller for training and validation notes
records.labeller_eval_evidence: 'the rule-based approach had even higher recall, identifying 125 notes (87%)' on the manually reviewed test set.
records.statistical_test: McNemar's test of homogeneity against the rule-based approach's predictions
records.null_stated: implied (no difference from the rule-based labeller)
records.gold_positives_value: 143 positive notes; 19 positive patients
records.notes: One of the few papers whose statistical test is explicitly a comparison with the weak labeller itself. Inter-rater agreement 0.98. Small test cohort acknowledged without an MDE.

records.venue: Proceedings (IEEE International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedicine)
records.title: Deep Learning Identification of Asthma Inhaler Techniques in Clinical Notes
records.labeller_type: handcrafted keyword rules (MedTaggerIE) labelling 27,363 notes for distant supervision
records.labeller_eval_evidence: Rules were 'evaluated against manual chart review as a gold standard', but the quality of the weak labels on the 27,363 distantly supervised notes is not reported.
comparator_names: BERT (trained on the small manual set)
records.statistical_test: none; point estimates only
records.prevalence_value: 0.7% sentence-level positives in the test set
records.notes: Companion paper to Agnikula Kshatriya 2021 (BMC MIDM) using the same corpus; see sensitivity analysis. Prevalence of 0.7% with no interval and no MDE.

records.venue: eGEMs (Generating Evidence and Methods to improve patient outcomes)
records.title: Extracting Patient-Centered Outcomes from Clinical Notes in Electronic Health Records: Assessment of Urinary Incontinence After Radical Prostatectomy
records.labeller_type: domain dictionary of affirmative UI expressions used to build an artificial training set
records.labeller_eval_evidence: Only the tool's output is scored 'against an unseen gold standard manually annotated by our board-certified Urology nurse'; the dictionary labeller is not separately validated. Gold set size inconsistent in the text (200 records vs 200 sentences).
comparator_names: none for the labelling stage; EPIC-26 patient-reported outcome used for concordance only
records.statistical_test: repeated-measures ANOVA and Student t-test for prevalence/means; kappa p-values
records.notes: The only record reporting a power figure ('we achieved a power of 0.84, which is considered adequate'), and it is a post-hoc power statement for the EHR-vs-EPIC-26 concordance analysis, not for the labeller evaluation. Companion study to Banerjee 2019 (JAMIA Open).

records.title: Biomedical literature mining: graph kernel-based learning for gene-gene interaction extraction
records.labeller_type: distant supervision from KEGG PATHWAY (gene pairs interacting in KEGG = positive)
records.labeller_eval_evidence: No evaluation of the KEGG-derived labels against manual annotation; the paper asserts only that 'the feasibility of the distant supervision method has been proven'.
records.statistical_test: McNemar test (WLK vs NHK, P = 3e-8)
records.prevalence_value: 25% by sampling design (1:3 positive:negative)
records.gold_positives_value: 10,500 distant-supervision positives; no manually annotated gold positives reported
records.notes: Evaluation uses distantly supervised labels as the reference, so there is no human gold standard at all.

records.venue: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making
records.title: Identification of asthma control factor in clinical notes using a hybrid deep learning model
records.labeller_type: handcrafted keyword rules (MedTaggerIE) producing weak labels for 27,363 notes
records.labeller_eval_evidence: Rules 'evaluated against manual chart review as a gold standard' (F1 0.837); the quality of the weak labels on the distant-supervision set is not reported.
records.statistical_test: none
records.prevalence_value: 0.56% sentence-level presence of inhaler techniques in the test set
records.notes: 'We observed some inconsistency in manual annotation' which was reconciled, but no agreement statistic. Companion paper to the 2020 IEEE BIBM study.

records.title: Weakly supervised temporal model for prediction of breast cancer distant recurrence
records.labeller_type: a previously published neural probabilistic NLP model used to weakly label 7,437 patients at two probability thresholds
records.labeller_eval_evidence: 'The NLP method scored 0.9 AUROC for detecting the recurrence timeline of the test data' (0.82 specificity, 0.73 sensitivity), cited to the authors' prior publication; the 7,437 weakly labelled patients are not evaluated.
comparator_names: XGBoost on a single vectorized note
records.statistical_test: none; values reported as 0.94 +/- 0.04 without defining the dispersion measure
records.notes: Patient counts inconsistent in the text (7,437 vs 8,062). Mean inter-annotator agreement 0.81.

records.venue: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making
records.title: A framework for extraction of clinical information from radiological mammography reports using large language models and retrieval augmented generation
records.labeller_type: GPT-4o-mini / GPT-4.1-mini few-shot entity and relation extraction with retrieved examples; output promoted into the pipeline as structured JSON
records.labeller_eval_evidence: Scored against manual annotation with strict offset matching: 'A prediction is counted as a True Positive (TP) only if the start character offset'.
records.statistical_test: none; five perturbation runs with standard deviation
records.gold_positives_value: held-out test set of 453 reports; per-class entity and relation counts not reported
records.notes: Dual independent annotation described but no agreement statistic reported.

records.title: Weak-Supervision Expectation-Maximization Framework for Identifying Decisional Vulnerability in Older Emergency Department Patients
records.text_domain: ED triage records + LLM-classified free-text chief complaints
records.labeller_type: labelling functions over structured triage features plus an LLM chief-complaint classifier, combined by an EM label model; logistic regression trained on the probabilistic labels
records.labeller_eval_evidence: EM output evaluated on a holdout set of definitive labels with bootstrap CIs; the LLM component checked against manual annotation (kappa 0.793).
records.statistical_test: bootstrap 95% CIs (1000 iterations); one-way ANOVA and chi-square for group comparisons
records.null_stated: partly (no group difference for ANOVA/chi-square); not stated for the labeller comparison
records.prevalence_value: 335/708 = 47.3% definitive labels; holdout ~47.2%
records.gold_positives_value: 335 (full definitive set); 134 in the holdout (derived from the confusion matrix)
records.notes: Says performance 'remained above chance' after ablation but reports no chance baseline. The LLM-removal ablation is the closest thing in the sample to a metadata-only alternative explanation, and it reduces AUC by 0.067 without any interval on the difference. Limitation acknowledged: 'the relatively small number of definitively labeled cases'.

records.title: Scalable Identification of Clinically Relevant Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Documents in Large-Scale Electronic Health Record Datasets With a Lightweight Natural Language Processing Model: Retrospective Cohort Study
records.labeller_type: ICD-code heuristics applied to 20,000 notes to produce silver training labels
records.labeller_eval_evidence: 'The defined ICD-based heuristics were evaluated against manually annotated gold-standard test data'; the silver labels themselves are not separately evaluated.
records.statistical_test: none; 95% bootstrap CIs for F1 (1000 iterations). Text claims the model 'significantly outperformed' the baseline without a test.
records.prevalence_value: ~67% (149/223) in the test set, derived from confusion matrices; not stated for the 307-document gold set
records.gold_positives_value: 149 derived for the 223-document test set; not stated for the gold set
records.notes: Here the ICD/metadata baseline IS the label source, so beating it is not an independent alternative-explanation test; three clinicians annotated with adjudication but no agreement statistic.

records.title: A weakly supervised transformer for rare disease diagnosis and subphenotyping from EHRs with pulmonary case studies
records.text_domain: EHR codified features + NLP features from notes
records.labeller_type: KOMAP silver labels, iteratively refined with model predictions
records.labeller_eval_evidence: 'Binary labels obtained by thresholding the initial silver-standard probabilities generated by KOMAP' are scored against held-out gold as a baseline; no labeller-only evaluation on the silver cohort.
records.statistical_test: 95% CIs from 1000-resample bootstrap; log-rank test and Cox HRs for the survival analysis
records.null_stated: partly (survival: no difference between clusters; HR = 1)
records.prevalence_value: PH 69/106 = 65%; severe asthma 52/99 = 53% in held-out sets
records.gold_positives_value: 69 (PH); 52 (severe asthma)
records.notes: No formal test between methods and the CIs overlap substantially (WEST 0.93 [0.87-0.97] vs KOMAP 0.86 [0.79-0.92]), which is exactly the situation an MDE statement would discipline. 'We allow this set to be small to ensure that the WEST pipeline is label-efficient.'

records.venue: Machine Learning for Healthcare Conference (MLHC) 2022; arXiv preprint
records.title: Classifying Unstructured Clinical Notes via Automatic Weak Supervision
records.verified_against: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.12088 (title, authors, and Comments field stating acceptance at MLHC 2022)
records.labeller_type: automatically generated keyword labelling functions + Snorkel data programming (KeyClass)
records.labeller_eval_evidence: 'Label Model accuracies are reported on the training set' for the non-clinical benchmarks; for MIMIC-III the labeller's own accuracy is not clearly reported.
records.statistical_test: none; '95% bootstrap confidence intervals'
records.prevalence_value: per-category prevalence 0.003-0.685 (Table 4); units inconsistent between text and table
records.gold_positives_value: test set 13,181 notes; positive counts not reported
records.notes: 'Label Model (Majority Vote)' is LF aggregation, not a majority-class baseline.

records.title: CheXpert: A Large Chest Radiograph Dataset with Uncertainty Labels and Expert Comparison
records.verified_against: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.07031 (title, 20 authors, 'Published in AAAI 2019', submitted 21 Jan 2019)
records.text_domain: radiology report text used to label chest radiographs
records.labeller_type: rule-based labeler (mention extraction, mention classification, mention aggregation)
records.labeller_eval_evidence: 1,000 reports annotated by two radiologists with consensus resolution: 'The resulting annotations serve as ground truth on the report evaluation set.' F1 mention 0.969 micro / 0.948 macro; negation 0.952/0.899; uncertainty 0.848/0.770.
records.statistical_test: for the labeller: none named (the word 'significantly' is used without a test). DeLong with Benjamini-Hochberg is used for the downstream uncertainty-handling AUCs.
records.prevalence_value: prevalence is reported for the training set only (Table 1)
records.gold_positives_value: 1,000 reports in the evaluation set; per-observation positive counts not given
records.notes: The field-defining case: the labeller is certified by absolute per-task F1 on 1,000 reports plus a comparison with one earlier labeller, with no interval, no stated null, and no per-class positive counts. Radiologists annotated independently but no agreement statistic is reported.

records.title: Combining Automatic Labelers and Expert Annotations for Accurate Radiology Report Labeling Using BERT
records.labeller_type: rule-based CheXpert labeler output used as training labels for BERT, then fine-tuned on expert annotations
records.labeller_eval_evidence: The CheXpert labeler is scored on the radiologist-labelled MIMIC-CXR test set: 'CheXpert, which achieves a score of 0.743' (95% CI 0.719-0.764).
comparator_names: Radiologist benchmark (one of two radiologists, F1 0.805)
records.statistical_test: nonparametric percentile bootstrap (1000 replicates) for CIs; paired bootstrap differences in F1 vs CheXpert, p<0.001
records.prevalence_value: prevalence reported for the CheXpert training set only (Table B1)
records.gold_positives_value: 687 gold reports; per-class positive counts not reported
records.notes: Methodologically the strongest labeller-level inference in the sample: paired bootstrap against another labeller with CIs. Still no prevalence, no per-class positive counts, and no MDE.

records.title: Large language models are few-shot clinical information extractors
records.text_domain: clinical notes (CASI, medication extraction, coreference, status classification)
records.labeller_type: GPT-3 plus a resolver; outputs on CASI used as weak supervision to train a smaller model
records.labeller_eval_evidence: The GPT-3+resolver labeller is scored against gold on each task and compared with prior systems.
records.statistical_test: none; results averaged over 5 one-shot example sets
records.gold_positives_value: 340 medication-status pairs; 100 coreference pairs for evaluation
records.notes: The strongest counter-example to the 'chance only' framing: it is the one paper in the sample that reports BOTH a random-guessing and a majority-class baseline, and it still reports no interval, no stated null and no MDE. Cohen kappa 0.59 is quoted for a prior dataset, not for its own annotations.

records.title: Large language models to identify social determinants of health in electronic health records
records.labeller_type: GPT-3.5-generated synthetic sentences labelled by their generation prompt category, used to augment fine-tuning data
records.labeller_eval_evidence: Generated sentences were human-reviewed ('after human review only 480 were found to have any SDoH mention') but no accuracy of the generated labels against gold is reported.
records.statistical_test: bootstrap 95% CIs (3400 and 10000 resamples); Mann-Whitney U p-values; chi-square and two-proportion z tests for bias analyses
records.prevalence_value: any SDoH ~2.6% (278/10,860 sentences); adverse SDoH ~0.9% (99/10,860), both derived from Table 5
